input:
We enabled GICv3.3 Non-Maskable Interrupts (NMI) for our hardware watchdog on an ARM Cortex-A78AE safety-island, but the watchdog NMI is not being delivered during a kernel spinlock critical section. The system eventually triple-faults instead of entering the NMI handler.

dmesg (before hang):
  [   1.200] GICv3: FEAT_NMI supported, GICD_TYPER.NMI=1
  [   1.201] GICv3: IRQ 42 (watchdog-bark) configured as NMI, priority=0x00
  [   1.202] GICv3: GICD_INMIR0 = 0x00000400 (SPI 42 marked non-maskable)

Register dump at hang:
  ICC_PMR_EL1  = 0x00  (all priorities masked!)
  PSTATE.ALLINT = 1     (ALLINT set — NMI supermask active)
  ICC_CTLR_EL1.PMHE = 0
  DAIF = 0x3C0 (IRQ+FIQ masked)

The kernel spinlock path calls local_irq_disable() which on this platform also sets PSTATE.ALLINT=1 via the ALLINT MSR. This effectively suppresses even NMI-priority interrupts. The watchdog bark fires at PMR priority 0x00 but ALLINT overrides PMR-based NMI delivery. How should we configure the system so that the watchdog NMI is truly non-maskable even during spinlock critical sections?
